title: Derived, Not Measured: The Category Error in Doubly Labeled Water Methodology
content: The doubly labeled water (DLW) method is routinely described as measuring total energy expenditure. This description is a category error. DLW measures the differential elimination rates of deuterium and oxygen-18, from which carbon dioxide production (rCO2) is estimated, from which total energy expenditure is derived using assumed respiratory quotients and stoichiometric coefficients. The 2021 consensus paper by Speakman and colleagues seeks to standardize this derivation. It is a careful and valuable contribution. It is also an unintentional demonstration of the problem: the paper reports that different equations introduce considerable variability, that the estimated rCO2 is sensitive to the dilution space ratio, and that the dilution space ratio varies non-linearly with body mass. These are not anomalies. They are the predictable consequences of treating a derived abstraction as if it were a measurement. The solution is not a better equation for TEE. The solution is to report the mass flux that DLW actually measures. The authors' database already contains that data. The conversion to energy is a choice, and it is a choice that introduces avoidable uncertainty. The body does not process energy. It processes mass. The methodology should reflect that reality.
